runners_data.name: Bogha Baiste
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in the spring before finishing fourth beaten 11 lengths at Kelso most recently in a novice hurdle. Returns off a break and handles good to soft; should find extra distance of benefit as he develops, with a midfield effort the realistic expectation here.

runners_data.name: Liberty Coach
runners_data.comment: Back after nearly four months away, having finished a 4.5-length third at Sedgefield on his last outing. A useful Flat performer who likes to race prominently over hurdles; first-time cheekpieces and better ground could help him show more consistent form on his return.

runners_data.name: Luckie Devil
runners_data.comment: Off the track for over four months after a series of pulled-up efforts, including at Ayr most recently in a novice hurdle. Has much still to find at this level, though acts on good ground and returns with a break behind him.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.comment: Travelled smoothly at the front last time at this track, going down by just a head in a handicap hurdle. Consistent and suited to this trip; first-time tongue-tie applied, though yet to get off the mark despite clear ability.

runners_data.name: Starshine Legend
runners_data.comment: Has a Flat success to his name and made a solid start over hurdles, finishing third 15 lengths back at Uttoxeter on debut. Good ground suits; more is expected with that run in the bank and our figures make him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Moon Reign
runners_data.comment: Struggled in a maiden on his latest start and holds little in the way of credentials for this grade; returning after a lengthy absence adds to the uncertainty. Trainer in good form is about the best that can be said; much to prove.

runners_data.name: Try Them
runners_data.comment: Showed decent form in Ireland before an unplaced effort on his most recent outing at Kilbeggan. Makes his stable debut here, which brings uncertainty; acts on soft and better may be expected if he adjusts to new surroundings.

runners_data.name: Dotties Promise
runners_data.comment: Landed a bumper success but has struggled to build on that over hurdles, no better than fourth in recent starts. Returns off a break; acts on good ground at 2m and needs to find more if she is to get involved.

runners_data.name: Clanokre Lass
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise on debut when fourth beaten eight lengths at Clonmel in a maiden hurdle, and that form has since been given added substance. She should progress further with a strong yard behind her; acts on good ground and handles this trip.

runners_data.name: Quinnfinity
runners_data.comment: Has pulled up in both her starts to date and given no real indication of ability in this grade. Returning off a break with first-time tongue-tie applied; everything still to show and ranks last on our figures.

races.name: Kettle Produce Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Pergamon
runners_data.note: Two wins on the bounce at 2m on Good ground are directly relevant here, and William Shanahan's 5lb claim helps offset a rising mark; headgear (tongue-tie) retained, 53 days off is within acceptable range, and though tagged as racing out of a pure prominent role, his natural front-running tendencies make him the dominant pace figure in this field.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back winner who took a handicap hurdle at Ludlow last time by two lengths, returning after a short break. Gone up 7lb for that effort but effective at 2m on a sound surface and could continue to progress on summer ground; a clear threat.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Recorded his sole win over this exact course and distance combination on Soft, and his Good-ground form is patchier (sim-going 12/15 suggests it's not a concern but not a clincher); Peter Kavanagh rides for a yard with just one runner in the past fortnight, and Pure Gold's prominent style means he gets a natural position here tracking Pergamon.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 18 lengths when fourth at this track last time, though she has been successful here and clearly handles the course. Still 4lb above her last winning mark; handles 2m on a sound surface and can go close if back to her best.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine has been active recently (4 wins from 26 in 14 days) and Danny McMenamin is a booking worth noting; form string 3549-3 includes a recent placed effort on Good, and though this horse genuinely wants to race prominently, Pergamon and Pure Gold are ahead of him in the pecking order for that position and he may find himself shuffled wider and further back than he'd like — b-headgear retained.
runners_data.comment: Third here 25 days ago, beaten just over four lengths in a handicap hurdle — a reliable campaigner who clearly handles this track and distance. First-time blinkers for a trainer in good form; effective on both soft and good ground and heads our ratings.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up runner alongside Tigress Lilly with no redistribution flag, so Just Dottie can at least race in her natural position; William Maggs' 3lb claim is useful, and her record shows a win on Soft at 13f — a step up from today's 2m minimum — meaning the trip may be on the sharp side for her style to be fully effective.
runners_data.comment: Unable to sustain the gallop here last time but stayed on to finish, still beaten without landing a blow in a handicap hurdle. Shows a consistent record at this track over 2m on good ground; needs to find more but holds realistic claims if she improves on latest.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: Form figures on Good ground this season (6,11) are poor, and her sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 4 runs on Good) raises a genuine flag; Alan Doyle's 3lb claim helps slightly but Tigress Lilly has yet to show she can compete off this sort of pace shape, and t-headgear has not unlocked an improvement so far.
runners_data.comment: Lost her place when the pace lifted here last time, comfortably held on her second run after a wind operation. Could do better given a more forward ride; first-time tongue-tie applied, though recent figures put her up against it.

runners_data.name: Interchangeable
runners_data.note: John Dixon trains and rides (7lb claim) this hold-up type who has finished in the frame on Good and Good-to-Soft at distances up to 18f; genuinely wants to be held up and deliver late, but with Pergamon likely to control pace and no pressure forcing a true burn-up, this horse's redistribution to a midfield position reflects reality — he simply won't get far enough back to deliver the run he needs, reducing his effectiveness materially.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Hexham last time on a trip that appeared too short, a horse rated reasonably on older Irish form but labelled unreliable. Acts on soft and good and handles this distance but hard to trust with any confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Pergamon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Pure Gold likely to push for early prominence, will be allowed to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m at Perth. Pure Gold will attempt to sit just off the pace in second or third, creating a tight, compressed lead group with no real pressure applied through the middle stages — a pattern that rewards the horse able to quicken from a handy position rather than grind from out the back. Ravenscraig Castle and Interchangeable are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively but, with Pergamon and Pure Gold already filling the front two berths, both are likely to find themselves racing in a more restrained position than suits their natural game. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting honest but not brutal fractions — strongly favours prominent/handy racers who can travel smoothly and pounce between the last two flights, rather than hold-up horses requiring a true searching pace to close the gap. This field contains more pace-seeking types than the race shape can accommodate: Ravenscraig Castle is the most likely prominent racer to actually secure that position, with Interchangeable likely unable to get close enough to exploit a late challenge.

watchPoints.text: Pergamon has won twice at 2m on Good recently and controls the pace entirely — if he jumps cleanly and is allowed to bowl along uncontested, the race is effectively his to give away.

Ravenscraig Castle's true nature as a prominent racer means Danny McMenamin may push forward early regardless of the mapped position — watch for a challenge for the front rank in the first half-mile that could briefly heat up the pace before settling.

Just Dottie is the hold-up runner best placed to benefit if the pace quickens unexpectedly, but William Maggs must find a clear run at the last — a compact field of six at Perth can compress and block late runners easily.

Tigress Lilly's Good-ground form (0 from 4 on similar going, sim-going 4/7) is a concern worth monitoring in-running — if she is struggling to go the pace from the outset, discount any latent market confidence.

Pure Gold's trainer has had only one runner in the past 14 days — low volume can occasionally signal a specific target race, worth noting if Pure Gold drifts or shortens sharply in the ring before the off.

races.name: Secure Air Parks Edinburgh Airport Parking Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer for Lisa Harrison and Danny McMenamin who has placed four times on Good in recent starts at 2m4f and 3m, and the course-distance form here is directly relevant; 25 days since last run is fine and the p-headgear suits, but he needs a genuinely contested pace to close into.
runners_data.comment: Familiar with the track and handles the trip and going, but has been well below his best in recent starts, beaten 21 lengths when fourth here last time. First-time cheekpieces could be the prompt for a revival; heads the ratings.

runners_data.name: Gunnery Sergeant
runners_data.note: The only natural front-runner in this field; Gordon Elliott has had seven runners in the past 14 days suggesting strong current form, and Sean Bowen is a high-calibre booking — uncontested on the lead over this Good-ground 2m4f trip, his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is racing closer to the front than usual on the map, but here he actually gets his preferred role.
runners_data.comment: Has shown fair form over hurdles with second-place finishes in recent starts and now gets his first crack at a handicap over fences for a capable yard. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces added; effective between 2m and 2m4f with cut and with more to offer at this level.

runners_data.name: Moodofthemoment
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 2m on Good for Sean Quinlan and David Thompson, returning just 11 days later which suggests confidence from connections; races from the rear and his sim-going record of 2W4P on good ground is the strongest in the field, so if there's any kick at the end of this trip he is a serious factor.
runners_data.comment: Third 16 lengths adrift at Hexham on his most recent outing, he has run at this course and distance before and knows the track. The sound surface suits and first-time cheekpieces could sharpen focus, though his inconsistent record makes him a risk.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: Experienced Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore-trained ten-year-old with a solid sim-going record of 1W7P; his true running style is hold-up but the density of hold-up horses in this race has pushed him onto the map further forward than he would naturally race — he will need cleaner air than this shape is likely to offer, which tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Never got into contention and finished 13 lengths back in third at this track last time, needing to bounce back from that effort. Trainer in good form and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied; best at 2m but handles this trip on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose best form has come over 2m on soft ground — the Good going and step up to 2m4f both represent slight stretches — trainer Leonard Kerr has had no runners in the past 14 days, and while the redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded back end of this field, his genuine style is rear-of-the-field.
runners_data.comment: Shaped as if the shorter trip was against him in a handicap hurdle here last time, and the step back up in distance looks vital. Winless of late and last on our figures, though handles the going and extra yardage could unlock more.

runners_data.name: Button Rock
runners_data.note: Six-year-old Elliott runner who returns after 51 days off with a poor recent form string of 8050-6; his sim-going record on Good shows no wins from three runs, and his natural hold-up style is displaced by the congestion in this field — the layoff and weak form make him the hardest to back in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Faded and was never within striking distance in a handicap hurdle last time out; without a win in recent starts. Making his chasing debut on a fair Irish-form mark; handles this distance and worth noting if the market speaks in his favour.

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner but included in the data; his form of F44-11 shows back-to-back wins on Good at 2m-2m1f which is eye-catching, and his true style is hold-up, pushed forward on the map only because of field congestion — if he does run, the recent winning form and good-ground sim record of 2W2P make him a live contender in any scenario where the pace quickens late.

races.paceDynamic: Gunnery Sergeant is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rivals likely to press for the lead, Sean Bowen can dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m4f trip on Good ground at Perth. The field behind him is dominated by hold-up horses — Wasdell Dundalk, Moodofthemoment, Garde Des Champs, Kinbara Firstdraft, Button Rock and Jiair Madrik all prefer to race off the pace — meaning Gunnery Sergeant faces no meaningful early pressure and can set his own terms throughout. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear, with Garde Des Champs, Kinbara Firstdraft and Jiair Madrik all redistributed to midfield positions they would not naturally occupy, meaning crowding behind the leader is likely and getting a clear run will be a premium. This race shape — an uncontested leader controlling a steady pace through the early stages — strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles, with hold-up horses needing significant late momentum that an unhurried gallop may simply not generate.

scenarios.title: Gunnery Sergeant Dominates

scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces

scenarios.body: If the redistributed hold-up types who are mapped to midfield manage to secure a forward position and race closer than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference disrupt the order and the race degenerates into a scramble in the straight.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or interference disrupt the order and the race degenerates into a scramble in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Gunnery Sergeant sets a very controlled pace on Good ground — watch whether any of the hold-up pack, particularly Moodofthemoment, can generate enough momentum off such a slow tempo to mount a genuine challenge.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Garde Des Champs, Kinbara Firstdraft and Button Rock — will all be seeking similar racing room turning for home; congestion and interference in the straight is a real risk that could compromise more than one runner's chance.
Jiair Madrik's non-runner status needs confirming at the final declaration stage — if he does line up, his two recent wins on Good ground alter the competitive picture materially.

Moodofthemoment returning just 11 days after his last run is worth monitoring in the paddock; connections clearly feel he is in form but the quick turnaround on Good ground over a longer 2m4f trip is a stamina query worth watching in the early exchanges.

Button Rock's 51-day absence for Gordon Elliott — who has been very active in the past 14 days — could mean a fitness question or simply a delayed entry; watch for market support as a guide to whether the stable feels he is ready.

races.name: PWA Architecture Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sonyourastar
runners_data.note: Hold-up style for Olly Murphy and Sean Bowen, but flagged for fading in the finish — 0 wins and 0 places from 3 sim-going runs, and a form string of 344-88 suggests this OR 99 rating may be flattering current ability; 41 days off is not a concern but the lack of a finish is.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts, he has looked in need of a longer trip in recent outings; makes his handicap debut wearing a tongue-tie for the first time, and this step up in distance on ground he handles gives him a genuine chance of improvement.

runners_data.name: Fourofakind
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan partners a natural hold-up horse who has good sim-going form (6th of 15 runs, 2W 2P at 20f on Good) and has been off 102 days — the break is the key question mark, though Lizzie Quinlan's yard is cold (0/9 in 14 days) and the P in recent form at this sort of trip needs explaining.
runners_data.comment: Rates third on our figures and handles both today's trip and going, returning from a break fitted with cheekpieces for the first time; a prolonged run of disappointing efforts and a mark that has been working against him are the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Bayonetta
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent runner with excellent sim-going figures (11 runs, 6 places on Good) and consistent placed form at 20-24f; Benjamin Macey takes a 5lb claim which helps at OR 97, and the step back to a truly confirmed Good surface at Perth suits this horse's profile well.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated here and generally reliable in her recent starts, she came up second last time on a shorter trip than she prefers; steps back up to a distance she handles in first-time cheekpieces, and her consistent profile makes her the one they all have to beat.

runners_data.name: Betteryouthanme
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was an OR 94 winner 16 days ago over 2m on Good and returns just 11 days later for R Mike Smith — the stable has recent form (2/23 in 14 days) and this horse clearly thrives on Good ground (4 from 6 in sim-going), making the quick turnaround a live angle rather than a concern.
runners_data.comment: Won here off a lower mark at the penultimate start and ran creditably when third last time at the same official rating as today; in form and handles this trip and going, making him a fair each-way prospect at a mark that looks workable.

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: Prominent-style five-year-old who won over 2m on Good and comes back 11 days later — sim-going record is solid (12/15, 1W 4P) but the step up to 2m4f and the P in recent form are untested questions; trainer David Thompson is cold (0/3 in 14 days) and the conditional Joshua Thompson is on.
runners_data.comment: Landed this race last year and ran fifth on his return 11 days ago; the step up in trip looks the key angle — he was comfortably held last time in a race that didn't play to his strengths — and first-time cheekpieces could help him travel better.

runners_data.name: Lenko
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Gordon Elliott (9/65 T14 — yard is active) with a fade flag — just three career runs, all on Good or similar, with 0 wins and 0 places; the four-year-old is still learning and 48 days off adds uncertainty, making this a development runner rather than a winning threat at present.
runners_data.comment: Twice unplaced and sixth in his three most recent starts, yet he rates second on our figures; the case rests on this handicap debut over a longer trip with first-time cheekpieces, which fits his profile as a likely improver once the step up in distance is granted.

runners_data.name: Fairly Fulling
runners_data.note: Prominent runner, eight years old, who won over 2m on Soft and has consistent placed form at 20-24f on various surfaces; Susan Corbett's yard is cold (0/4) and the sim-going record (7/15, 0W) lacks a win in similar conditions, but the horse plugs on and keeps finding the frame.
runners_data.comment: Holds some form claims over this trip and going, and was travelling well before fading in the closing stages last time; the combination of tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time is a potential plus, but his ranking outside the top eight makes him harder to recommend.

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: Jonathon Bewley partners a seven-year-old who is a true hold-up horse — the redistribution note means this horse is likely to find itself racing further forward than it wants given the volume of similar types in the field, which compromises its style_fit (0.91) and tempers confidence; one placed run from 6 on Good is modest.
runners_data.comment: Back to something like his best when runner-up here last time off a 3lb lower mark, and rates fourth on our figures; wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time and should be suited by the step up in distance, though his inconsistent record is the main reservation.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Lisa Harrison, uncontested on paper today — 11 years old but consistent (5 placed runs from 11 on sim-going, 1 win) and returned just 11 days ago; the key question is whether this well-handicapped veteran on OR 81 can convert consistent placing into a win when allowed to control the race entirely.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of his last two completions and shaped creditably at Hexham on his most recent outing from a prominent position; yet to win in his last six starts but his figures look fair and he is back running to something like his best.

runners_data.name: Breaking Ground
runners_data.note: Five-year-old true hold-up horse with a fading flag — form string P50-08 is stark, and the redistribution means this horse is unlikely to secure its natural position at the back; sim-going record (4/7, 0W 0P) and a 25-day return do little to build a case, making this hard to endorse.
runners_data.comment: Failed to see out the trip here last time and her recent record is generally inconsistent; she has shown ability at shorter distances on going that suits, and a first-time hood may help, but she faces a stiff task on these figures.

runners_data.name: Dreamings Free
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Charlie Price and Maurice Barnes (yard 0/1 in 14 days) returning from 192 days off — the long break is a significant flag, and though the horse has placed at 24f on Soft and Good (0W 1P from 7 sim-going runs), being pushed out of a true back-of-field position by the volume of hold-up types in this race compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Disappointed when stepped back up in trip at Musselburgh on his most recent outing, with form tailing off sharply towards the end of last season; returns from 192 days off with a first-time hood and handles the trip and going, but is the lowest-rated in the field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Malangen is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the outset at a sustainable clip on Good ground over 2m4f at Perth, a track that rewards accuracy and jumping rather than raw galloping speed. With no genuine rival to press Malangen for the lead, expect a measured, controlled tempo that keeps the race together until the final circuit, where the pace will lift organically. The field behind is heavily populated by prominent and hold-up types — Bayonetta, Betteryouthanme, and Top Flight Century will look to track closely, while Sonyourastar, Fourofakind, and Lenko sit further back. This shape — a steady single leader, a compact chasing pack, and a late acceleration — strongly favours prominent racers with clean jumping and stamina who can sit just behind the leader and pick Malangen off in the straight, rather than true closers needing a strong gallop to close from deep. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: King Kodiak, Breaking Ground, and Dreamings Free are all natural hold-up horses, but with three of them present, only one or two can realistically secure that position; the others will find themselves racing more prominently than ideal, diluting their chance.

watchPoints.text: Betteryouthanme returns just 11 days after a win and has the best recent form of any prominent runner in this field — watch whether the quick turnaround dulls its effectiveness or it takes full advantage of tracking Malangen into a slow-run race.

Malangen's uncontested lead could turn this into a lottery from the final flight — watch the pace throughout, particularly at the top of the home straight, to see whether any prominent horse can apply enough pressure to force an error or a tired jump.

Bayonetta, Betteryouthanme, and Top Flight Century are all prominent-style runners and cannot all slot in immediately behind Malangen — watch for early positioning battles and potential crowding at the first hurdle that could unsettle the race shape.

King Kodiak, Breaking Ground, and Dreamings Free are all natural hold-up horses, and with all three present only one can realistically settle at the back; watch which, if any, does so cleanly — the others will be racing out of role and their form figures become less reliable as a result.

Dreamings Free returns from 192 days off and is worth monitoring in the early stages — a hold-up horse coming back from a long break in a race with limited pace is a volatile combination, and how it travels in the first half will reveal whether it is ready to run its race today.

races.name: Horizon Parking UK's Leading Parking Company Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: The Flying Poet
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with Sean Bowen and in-form Olly Murphy yard (5 wins from 12 in 14 days); excellent sim-going profile (9/10) and strong recent form (221-12) over comparable trips makes him the key pace influence, though OR 105 top weight is worth noting over this longer 3m trip.
runners_data.comment: Landed a short-head success at this venue two starts ago and remains consistent, though jumping errors cost him when runner-up last time off the same mark as today. Blinkers and tongue-tie applied; effective over 3m on a sound surface and the stiff test suits.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Blizzard
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for the Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore partnership; recent form figures of 2PP-57 are patchy and the sim-going record shows no wins from 15 attempts on Good, limiting confidence despite a relatively light weight of 163lbs.
runners_data.comment: Dropped in trip at Hexham last time in a handicap chase and was well beaten, a performance short of his best. Trainer in good form and first-time tongue-tie applied; effective over 3m on a sound surface and should be better served by today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Get A Superstar
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with back-to-back wins (5/7-11 culminating in two victories) over Good ground, and the trip of 3m is a step up he looks capable of handling; a natural prominent racer who should be able to secure a good early position behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back successes include taking a handicap by 5½ lengths at Market Rasen most recently, and his mark still looks lenient on his best earlier form. First-time cheekpieces applied; stamina over this longer trip is the main doubt, and his trainer's recent results have been modest.

runners_data.name: Thehairyfella
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran for Gordon Elliott with a strong sim-going record (13/15 on Good-type surfaces) and best run last time (4th over 26f on Good); genuine hold-up type who needs a proper stamina test to produce his best, and Danny McMenamin is an experienced handler of such animals.
runners_data.comment: Struggled to get into the race at Downpatrick last time, failing to travel throughout a handicap chase. Inconsistent but on a workable official mark; effective over 3m on a sound surface and first-time blinkers give reason for hope.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner dropped back to an attractive OR of 83 after a string of placed efforts; Nathan Moscrop's claim is noted but this horse has five consecutive places on Good ground suggesting consistency rather than a winning profile — one to respect rather than fear.
runners_data.comment: Went too hard too soon here last time in a handicap hurdle and paid the price, finishing well beaten. His French form hints at better ability on a fair mark; first-time tongue-tie fitted and more tactical restraint in running could help.

runners_data.name: Defying Gravity
runners_data.note: Carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish and is a true hold-up horse whose running style is compromised in this one-pace shape; Andrew Hamilton's runner has limited sim-going form (3/8) and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations — best watched for a more suitable pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Jumping and travelling were both problems at Cartmel last time, well beaten in a handicap hurdle. Switching to fences, where significant improvement is needed; acts around 2m on good to soft and first-time tongue-tie is the main positive.

runners_data.name: Twp Stori
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent-running type for Samuel Drinkwater but the crowded front end means this runner is unlikely to get close to its preferred berth early on; the recent form of 33 over comparable Good-ground trips suggests consistency at this level, but competing out of natural position reduces its winning prospects meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Dropped out and stayed on to finish third 13 lengths back at Uttoxeter last time on a surface faster than he ideally wants. A genuine stayer over 3m+ and fairly treated on his hurdle form; first-time cheekpieces applied, though softer conditions would suit better.

races.paceDynamic: The Flying Poet is the lone confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to push him across the first mile, he is able to dictate a sustainable, controlled tempo over this 3m trip on Good ground at Perth. Get A Superstar and Burgundy Man are natural prominent racers who will seek to press close behind, creating a compact but unhurried early gallop rather than a searching test. This shape — a measured pace with a single horse in control — classically rewards those able to track the leader from the front two or three positions, conserving energy before jumping the final bend fence and extending from the front. The field holds more prominent-to-front types than the map can naturally accommodate: The Flying Poet is best placed to secure the lead, with Get A Superstar and Burgundy Man the two most likely to achieve the next positions, meaning Twp Stori — a genuine prominent racer — is likely to find itself racing further back than it wants, and its chance is tempered accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Watch The Flying Poet at the early fences — if Sean Bowen can establish control without being pressed, the race could be over as a contest by the home turn on each circuit.

Get A Superstar's jockey Charlie Hammond must act decisively from the stalls to claim one of the two seats immediately behind the leader; if Burgundy Man or another prominent type crowds him out, his chance diminishes sharply.

Twp Stori's redistribution to midfield is a genuine tactical handicap — monitor whether Benjamin Macey (5lb claim) attempts to push forward regardless; if he does, the early gallop could quicken slightly and alter the scenario probabilities.

Thehairyfella's veteran stamina profile is worth monitoring from the third-last fence — if the pace has been sufficient to string the field out, he could be closing late and represents the most credible hold-up threat on sim-going figures.

Defying Gravity's fade tendency combined with 36 days off the track is a flag to watch if it travels prominently early — any signs of jumping errors or laboured movement between the final two fences would confirm the fading-in-finish concern.

races.name: AEJ Facilities Management Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Maggies Boy
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground (11/15 sim-going record) and a genuine hold-up horse suited to 3m; Sean Quinlan is a strong booking and a recent win at this distance over Good gives confidence, though the form string includes some poor runs and he needs the pace to collapse.|
runners_data.comment: Won by over three lengths at Sedgefield in April off a 2lb lower mark, but his chasing career has stalled since, with errors blighting his last two starts; handles this trip and going, and first-time cheekpieces may help him settle and complete, making midfield a realistic aim.

runners_data.name: Les's Legacy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has done most of his recent racing at shorter trips on Soft, and the switch back to Good and a step up to 3m both require optimism; Susan Corbett's T14 strike rate of 0/4 offers little encouragement and he carries blinkers and a cheekpiece combination suggesting the yard is searching for solutions.|
runners_data.comment: Briefly looked a threat at Hexham last time before fading out of contention; rates fourth on our figures, is down in the weights from recent runs, and wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time — but needs a more sustained effort than he has produced recently.

runners_data.name: Creadan Grace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has the standout recent form in the race — a win and a close third at this trip on Good ground — and the prominent style means Robert Dunne can sit in the ideal position tracking The Best Way; the T14 strike rate of 8/57 confirms the yard is firing and the 5/24f/GOO run latest is directly relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Has a win and a place from her recent starts, but was held up after going to the front too early at Perth last time; first-time cheekpieces may encourage a more patient ride, though her inconsistent profile remains a concern.

runners_data.name: The Best Way
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Nicky Richards' eight-year-old can control the race at the pace Danny McMenamin chooses on Good ground; form figures of 1 and two thirds suggest he is in decent order, though the step up from 17-20f to 3m is untested on Good and his sim-going record of 0W/1P at 2/8 gives some pause.|
runners_data.comment: Top-rated here and in consistent form — placed twice and with a win from his last four starts; shaped well at Uttoxeter on his most recent outing and handles today's going, suggesting his campaign is building with further improvement a realistic prospect.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up horse with a solid Good-ground record (11/15) and has placed at 3m on Good before; Lisa Harrison's T14 record of 0/1 is quiet and the age means this horse needs things to go perfectly, but the consistency in the form figures makes him a legitimate contender if the pace runs them all into the ground.|
runners_data.comment: Landed this contest last year and handles the going well, but was never competitive and faded badly when held last time at this course; generally consistent at this level and ideally wants even further than today's trip, though he has been without a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Loro White
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old won last time at 20f on Soft and holds genuine ability, but being a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the weight of runners at the rear means his natural race-reading is compromised here; Sean Bowen is a strong positive but the redistribution tempers confidence given the style fit of 0.92 out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Won here by four lengths off a 5lb lower mark at the penultimate start and rates second on our figures; shaped to her ability last time carrying the same official mark as today, and wears tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time — she may be even better suited going further.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: Derek Fox partners this five-year-old who has posted six consecutive finishes outside the frame; in nature a hold-up horse, here shunted into midfield alongside several others, and with a style fit of 0.90 suggesting it cannot race to its strengths, the modest form record and lack of any Good-ground win make it hard to make a case.|
runners_data.comment: Useful form in points and bumpers has not transferred to hurdles; his performances in this sphere have been consistently disappointing and he dropped out badly when stepped up in trip on handicap debut, though his trainer is in good form and he handles today's going.

runners_data.name: Prince Nino
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Soft in what looks a form upturn, but that victory came on Soft and the sim-going record on Good is 0W/1P from seven; a hold-up horse by nature, Alan Doyle (3) faces the challenge of getting position in a congested midfield, and 50 days off adds an element of fitness query to an already tricky profile.|
runners_data.comment: Back to his best when taking a handicap here by three and a half lengths last time off a 5lb lower mark, and he clearly acts well at this course; fitted with tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time and off a short break, though his inconsistent record is the main reservation.

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: Patrick Neville's seven-year-old runs just 11 days after its last start, which may indicate confidence in fitness, but a form string of 43P-75 and no wins from 15 runs on this type of going is damning; a true hold-up horse crowded into midfield by the field's composition, the redistribution leaves it racing in a compromised position at a long price.|
runners_data.comment: Tried to dominate at Hexham last time but made jumping errors and was reeled in, beaten six and a half lengths; handles this trip and going as a strong stayer, and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces may encourage a more settled approach, though she has been without a win in her recent starts.

runners_data.name: King Gold Boy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old off the track for 206 days — the longest absence in the field — trained by Jean McGregor, who has no T14 runners and therefore no current form lines to read; a hold-up horse in nature mapped to midfield, and a form string of PP/7P- on various surfaces provides no basis for confidence on return from a lengthy break.|
runners_data.comment: Has been pulled up three times in his last four starts over hurdles and has not yet struck upon conditions to show his best in this sphere; returns after 206 days off with a first-time hood and is difficult to recommend on these figures as the lowest-rated in the field.

races.paceDynamic: The Best Way is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 3m Perth handicap hurdle and, with no other genuine lead horse in the field, Danny McMenamin can dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits on Good ground. At 3m on Good, that is likely to be a steady-to-honest gallop rather than a lung-bursting affair, meaning The Best Way's lead will be uncontested and potentially very difficult to peg back in the home straight. The field contains a significant cluster of hold-up types — Loro White, C'Mon So, Prince Nino, Myfavouritesister and King Gold Boy are all true rear-to-midfield horses — but with five such runners and only one confirmed front-runner, several of them will be jostling for position further forward than their natural style and are unlikely to settle where they want; Creadan Grace, with a prominent tag and the best recent form in the race, is the likeliest to secure the position closest to The Best Way. The race shape strongly favours a front-runner or a single, well-positioned prominent horse who can track the pace and pounce at the last, rather than the swarm of hold-up types who face a long and potentially fruitless hunt from the rear.

watchPoints.text: The Best Way's jumping — McMenamin will be setting his own pace in front and any mistake at a hurdle could bring the field back to him and change the complexion entirely; watch the early fences to see if he travels fluently or gets in tight.

Crowded midfield positioning at the first few hurdles is a serious risk given five horses have been redistributed from their natural hold-up positions — Loro White, C'Mon So, Prince Nino, Myfavouritesister and King Gold Boy could all be caught in a pocket or forced wide on the first circuit.

Creadan Grace's price is likely to shorten significantly if The Best Way shows any signs of being caught cold at the start — Elliott's horse wants to travel prominently and needs a clear sightline; watch the draw and early positioning to see if Robert Dunne can sit directly behind the leader.

King Gold Boy returning after 206 days with Jean McGregor's limited recent evidence is a significant unknown — jumps horses that have been off that long frequently make jumping errors on return and could cause interference in a tightly bunched midfield.

Maggies Boy's form string includes a PU, suggesting jumping reliability is not guaranteed even if Sean Quinlan is in the plate; at 3m on Good, any jumping error in the home straight could cost a horse with hold-up running style that needs everything to go right.
